claim: GlucoSana is a German-language blood sugar capsule from the '-Sana' product family. It's built around chromium picolinate, which the page says is a missing 'key' for insulin receptors, plus berberine, curcumin, gymnema, alpha-lipoic acid, magnesium and vitamin D.
story: The page's own header refers to 'NerveSana' in places, a sign that the page was adapted from a sister product.
ing_note: The page describes a 10-ingredient formula and mentions a chromium dose of 100 mcg; other amounts aren't shown in text.
price_note: GlucoSana is sold in euro packages at roughly €47–67 per bottle depending on the package size; totals and shipping appear on the order page.
refund_note: The page refers to both 60- and 90-day guarantees; check which applies at checkout.
checks: Chromium deficiency is rare, and chromium supplements have small, inconsistent effects on blood sugar.
The historical figures about German chromium intake since 1876 aren't sourced.
Berberine has real blood sugar evidence, but its dose here isn't stated.
The FAQ asks whether you can reduce or stop diabetes medication; never do that without your doctor.
cons: Dose of key ingredients not shown
Copy-paste errors from a sister product
verdict: GlucoSana combines a few ingredients with some evidence and a lot of marketing. It can add to the effect of diabetes medicine, so monitor your blood sugar and involve your doctor. It isn't a replacement for treatment.
